What actually happened this week was behavioral: the book sat 100% flat for two full weeks (7/15 to 7/27) before finally opening BKR, which is now +3.13% and comfortably inside its trailing stop with the thesis intact. What went right -- every other researched candidate this week (MPC, NET, TRV, APH, ADI, AJG, S, TEAM, BSX) was passed on for a specific, named reason (earnings binary already priced by options, insider selling against a green candle, institutional distribution against a beat-pop) rather than vague caution, and BKR itself was a genuine, verified fat pitch rather than a forced trade to end the drought. What went wrong is the drought itself -- a two-week stretch of zero activity is the same standing-caution-becomes-policy failure CLAUDE.md's own 7/21 audit already documented, just recurring in a milder form, and it is a process risk, not a data problem.
